## Which Clover Time codes have been verified?

None have been tested in this session. Keep the structured codes array empty until there is evidence of successful redemption. Beebom and Game Rant provide research leads, not proof that a code still works.

On October 9, 2026, this author read [Destructoid's code article](https://www.destructoid.com/clover-time-codes/), credited to Ana Mitic and published and modified on October 8. Its list includes newer claims and differs from Beebom on expired entries and some reward quantities. The article date is not a successful-redemption record. Candidates and conflicting rewards stay in the project research ledger rather than the active or expired array.

The [public Trello Codes card](https://trello.com/c/Lyr4hnVN/75-codes) supplies another list with "Active" labels and short expiry dates. Its spellings and punctuation differ from some article lists, one code appears with two dates, and the dates omit the year and timezone. Those claims do not establish current validity or a reliable expiryDate value, so the structured array remains empty.

## What evidence is needed for each reward?

Record the original announcement, the exact code text, the test time, the response message, and the observed reward. Keep eligibility failures separate from expired-code evidence.

## Where will redemption instructions appear?

Link to the completed redemption guide after its actual UI path is tested. Do not duplicate code entries in this article body.

## What is this draft's evidence status?

This page is not ready for publication. See [the official Roblox experience](https://www.roblox.com/games/93934100402512/Clover-Time) for the developer's game description. > **Research preview.** This page contains source-attributed research, not a completed or independently play-tested guide. Unconfirmed steps and conflicting reports are marked below. Do not treat a reported code, cost, probability, or unlock condition as verified.

{/* P05: development research draft; excluded from production while draft is true. */}

![Original fantasy concept illustration for beginner guide, not gameplay footage](/images/articles/clover-time/beginner-concept.webp)

*Original concept artwork, not a Clover Time screenshot or a depiction of a verified route, weapon, or spell.*

![Original beginner systems overview explanatory diagram, not an in-game screenshot](/images/articles/clover-time/beginner-guide-overview.svg)

*Original explanatory diagram. Source context and unconfirmed details are explained below.*

## What does the official game description confirm?

The official Roblox description lists Grimoire progression, action combat, spell combos, awakenings, Magic Broom flight, Magic Squads, and AFK World rewards. It does not establish their unlock order. On October 8, 2026, the [official game API](https://games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=9891331827) labeled the game BETA 0.1; the player-wiki articles cited below do not identify which build their instructions describe.

## What should a new player do first?

Check the tutorial and quest prompts before spending resources. The reported tool and starter-chest routes below come from two articles on the same independent player wiki. This author has read those articles and inspected Gamepur's published screenshots, but has not tested the routes or watched the player wiki's underlying recordings.

The site's [reroll reference](https://clovertime.wiki/progression/clover-time-rerolls), read on October 9, 2026, distinguishes Race, Social Class, and Trait. Its class reference places Sovereign in Social Class; Chosen One belongs to its Trait list. Do not interpret these three categories as interchangeable names for a race or combat class.

## How are starter tools reportedly obtained?

According to the [player wiki's tool walkthrough](https://clovertime.wiki/gear/clover-time-how-to-get-tools), Lily stands outside the starting church and gives a free Rake when you accept her potato quest. The article says the Rake arrives equipped and that harvesting uses E beside a fully grown crop. Those details still need an independent interface check.

The same article reports that a lumberjack's firewood quest gives a free Axe in your inventory. It does not establish the lumberjack's exact name, a complete route from spawn, or the controls for equipping the Axe. This draft therefore cannot yet provide a complete tool-acquisition walkthrough.

The article connects potatoes with early quests and crafting, and wood with crafting. Specific recipes and quantities are outside the verified scope of this draft.

The [public Trello Lily quest card](https://trello.com/c/jnXF9mVh/237) names a four-potato gathering task with a level requirement of 3. A [Lucie quest card](https://trello.com/c/O1FZ4lEW/238) describes collecting five Wood for the church, but its Portuguese and English sections disagree on the level requirement. These are additional research leads, not proof of the tool handout: the board's Rake and Iron Hatchet acquisition fields are blank. Do not equate five Wood with five whole trees or assume Lucie is the unnamed tool-giving NPC without gameplay evidence.

## What is the reported first Grimoire route?

The [player wiki's Grimoire walkthrough](https://clovertime.wiki/magic/clover-time-how-to-get-grimoire) describes this opening sequence:

1. Open the starter Normal Chest, then its Medium Chest, to obtain a Mana Crystal.
2. Follow the compass tower icon to the Grimoire Tower.
3. Find the rolling point inside and check its current cost before accepting a roll.
4. After the animation, check your hand and inventory for the resulting Grimoire.

This is a third-party reported sequence, not a tested set of instructions. The article reports one Mana Crystal per roll and distinguishes that resource from Spins used for character rerolls. Read the current game prompt rather than assuming the reported cost remains unchanged.

The source also describes different tutorial states: some players receive a tower key from a nearby NPC, while others enter directly. The NPC's name and the conditions for those routes are unresolved. Manual equipment controls and the input for using a first spell are also missing, so this route does not yet meet the full beginner-guide acceptance criteria.

## What can actually be read at the tower?

[Gamepur's Grimoire guide](https://www.gamepur.com/guides/how-to-get-grimoire-clover-time), by Aleksa Stojković and published October 5, 2026, includes a tower screenshot inspected for this draft. A level-2 character stands at a red altar. The interaction reads **Grimoire Roll**, **E**, and **Read**, beside a blue crystal icon marked **x1**. The HUD build label is **v0.10.41-T**. This supports the displayed PC prompt and amount in that capture; it does not show pressing E, deducting currency, receiving a new book, or equipping it.

The same image displays guarantee denominators of **Epic 50, Legendary 100, and Mythic 250**, with a separate line saying **Roblox Plus · cuts every count by 30%**. [Roonby's October 2 guide](https://roonby.com/2026/10/02/how-to-get-a-grimoire-in-clover-time-guide/) lists 35, 70, and 175 without explaining that condition. Those numbers equal a 30% reduction of the pictured denominators, so they must not be presented as universal base guarantees. Whether that author used Plus is unknown. The capture does not prove how a counter resets or when a guarantee is awarded.

Gamepur also reports Menu → Inventory → select a Grimoire → Drop, a two-book default capacity, and a two-minute recovery window. These are written claims rather than inspected drop results. Dropping a book is not an established first-equipment step, and this draft does not recommend it.

[Destructoid's comparison article](https://www.destructoid.com/clover-time-tier-list/), published October 1, 2026 and modified October 6, reports another tower route: ask the starting village's Finral NPC for transport, or travel forward following compass headings between 105 and 120. This supplies a specific navigation lead from another publisher. This author has not checked the NPC, transport fee, heading reference, entrance, or whether that route fits the current spawn.

## Which resources should a beginner save?

Identify resources from the game interface and verify their uses before spending. Do not infer a crafting recipe, roll probability, or storage rule from another Roblox game. This draft makes no recommendation to reroll an existing character configuration or repeatedly spend Mana Crystals.

The [player wiki's Mana Crystal reference](https://clovertime.wiki/magic/clover-time-mana-crystals) repeats the starter-chest chain and distinguishes Mana Crystals for Grimoires from Spins for character attributes. It also reports conflicting potato quantities for crystal crafting, so this draft does not pick one quantity as the correct recipe. More pages on that same site are not independent confirmation.

## What does the public board report about broom travel?

The [Magic Broom card](https://trello.com/c/LzvDZm4Y/140-magic-broom) points to Master Elsie's mission; the [quest card](https://trello.com/c/e2s1xYsQ/259) names Learning to Fly and describes balance training for a first broom. Its location, exact interaction, conditions, and flight controls remain unverified by this author.

The [Finral card](https://trello.com/c/pqQhYTIT/327) describes paid travel to places already visited and includes the Grimoire Tower. This qualifies Destructoid's suggested teleport shortcut: it is not established as a free route to a new player's unvisited tower.

The tower and character-menu screenshots display **H — Spawn Broom**. That is a pictured PC control for those characters, not evidence that a new account already owns a broom or has completed Elsie's quest.

## What is this draft's evidence status?

This page is not ready for publication. See [the official Roblox experience](https://www.roblox.com/games/93934100402512/Clover-Time) for the developer's game description. The player-wiki tool and Grimoire walkthroughs were read on October 8, 2026; the other references and Gamepur screenshots were read or inspected on October 9. Gamepur and Roonby provide article dates, but their recordings' capture dates and current applicability remain unknown. Detailed claim records and unresolved steps are kept in the project's research documents.

## What should I read next?

These related pages are also research previews with their own evidence limits.

- [Source-attributed Grimoire comparisons](/guides/grimoire-tier-list/)

> **Research preview.** This page contains source-attributed research, not a completed or independently play-tested guide. Unconfirmed steps and conflicting reports are marked below. Do not treat a reported code, cost, probability, or unlock condition as verified.

{/* P09: development research draft; excluded from production while draft is true. */}

![Original fishing concept illustration, not gameplay footage](/images/articles/clover-time/fishing-concept.webp)

*Original concept artwork, not a Clover Time screenshot or a depiction of verified items, characters, locations, or mechanics.*

![Original keep activities distinct explanatory diagram, not an in-game screenshot](/images/articles/clover-time/fishing-fragments-overview.svg)

*Original explanatory diagram. Source context and unconfirmed details are explained below.*

## What evidence supports a fishing system?

The [player wiki's fishing article](https://clovertime.wiki/activities/clover-time-fishing), read on October 9, 2026, describes the activity, equipment, catch interaction, and rewards. That supports a specific third-party account, beyond the earlier code-reward lead. This author has not performed fishing or watched the article's claimed demonstrations.

## How is the activity unlocked and performed?

The article says a rod and bait are required. It reports village merchants selling both and a crafting-bench rod recipe, without a complete recipe or a standalone rod price. Its quoted shop price covers several listed items, so it cannot be used here as the cost of one rod.

The reported interaction is:

1. Equip the rod from inventory and approach river or sea water.
2. Press V to start fishing and choose bait.
3. Wait for a bite, then click through the catch minigame.
4. Check inventory for the fish.

This is a source-reported PC flow, not a verified route for every platform. Equipment inputs, exact minigame rules, failure conditions, merchant location, and current costs remain unresolved. The source alternates Hage and Haga for the village name across its articles, so no precise map route is accepted here.

## Are fragments actually part of the rewards?

The fishing article links Golden Marlin to Mana Crystal Fragments. The [same site's Mana Crystal reference](https://clovertime.wiki/magic/clover-time-mana-crystals) reports combining fragments and potatoes at a crafting bench, then using the whole crystal for Grimoire rolls.

These pages do not document how many fragments a catch yields or establish whether conversion needs another action. The Mana Crystal article reports conflicting potato quantities in its underlying accounts. This draft therefore does not give a definitive recipe, bait requirement for Golden Marlin, drop probability, or farming-speed estimate.

[Destructoid's comparison article](https://www.destructoid.com/clover-time-tier-list/), published October 1, 2026 and modified October 6, also connects fishing with progression materials. Its wording says fish can be used to craft Fragments and Mana Crystals, while the player wiki describes fragments from Golden Marlin catches. Destructoid also mentions enemy-derived fragments. Neither provides the complete conversion interface, so this draft does not collapse the two accounts into one confirmed catch-to-crystal procedure.

[Roonby's October 2 Grimoire guide](https://roonby.com/2026/10/02/how-to-get-a-grimoire-in-clover-time-guide/), by Jay, also names Golden Marlin as a fragment source without documenting the conversion. [Gamepur's October 5 Crystal Mana guide](https://www.gamepur.com/guides/how-to-get-crystal-mana-clover-time), by Aleksa Stojković, instead says successful fishing can yield a whole Crystal Mana. These reports leave the reward stage unresolved: they do not show whether a catch awards a crystal, an item must be converted, or a recipe must be crafted. This draft does not publish a guaranteed crystal-per-catch claim.

## Does the Crystal Mana screenshot show a fishing reward?

No. The in-article Gamepur image was actually inspected and depicts **AFK Rewards**, not fishing. It shows **+1 Spin every 15 minutes**, a **Random 2x Buff every 30 minutes**, and a **ONE TIME** weekly milestone of **3x Crystal Mana** at **168 hours**. This supports those pictured AFK labels only. It does not show a fishing catch or a milestone being claimed, and the ONE TIME label must not be turned into a recurring weekly promise.

## What does selling a fish reportedly do?

The source describes fish-dealer NPCs buying catches for game currency. Its currency spelling differs from the same site's Social Class reference. The current interface label, dealer's exact name, sale values, and transaction outcome still need a check; no "best money farm" claim is established here.

## Does the public board resolve the missing steps?

The [public Clover Time Trello board](https://trello.com/b/XHcUunD7) contains Fishing Rod, Golden Marlin, Crystal Mana Frags, and Mana Crystal cards. Their acquisition sections are blank or unfinished; the Fishing system card also has no instructions. Those names provide another reference point, but do not establish the Golden Marlin reward, rod purchase, equipment inputs, or conversion recipe. Blank template values are not accepted as documented item limits.

## What is this draft's evidence status?

This page remains a verification draft. The player-wiki articles have no inspected publication dates or linked original recordings. Destructoid supplies a named author and article dates, but no catch-to-crafting demonstration. Publication needs a current equipment and catch sequence, a Golden Marlin reward record, and a supported fragment-use step. All cited pages were read on October 9, 2026.

## What should I read next?

These related pages are also research previews with their own evidence limits.

- [First Grimoire route research](/guides/beginner-guide/)
- [Grimoire comparison research](/guides/grimoire-tier-list/)

> **Research preview.** This page contains source-attributed research, not a completed or independently play-tested guide. Unconfirmed steps and conflicting reports are marked below. Do not treat a reported code, cost, probability, or unlock condition as verified.

{/* P03: development research draft; excluded from production while draft is true. */}

![Original grimoires concept illustration, not gameplay footage](/images/articles/clover-time/grimoires-concept.webp)

*Original concept artwork, not a Clover Time screenshot or a depiction of verified items, characters, locations, or mechanics.*

![Original compare rankings by context explanatory diagram, not an in-game screenshot](/images/articles/clover-time/grimoire-tier-list-overview.svg)

*Original explanatory diagram. Source context and unconfirmed details are explained below.*

## Which Grimoires belong in this comparison?

The official description mentions Anti-Magic and other magic types without supplying a complete inventory roster. The [player wiki's Grimoire ranking](https://clovertime.wiki/tier-list/clover-time-grimoires-tier-list), read on October 9, 2026, lists ten books. Their names and placements below are source reports, not a roster observed by this author.

| Source's group | Reported Grimoires | Source's comparison |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tier I | Anti Magic; Poison | Its preferred PvE options, based on claimed damage and move variety. |
| Tier II | Ice; Explosive Flame; Battle Lightning | Alternatives it rates below its top group. |
| Tier III | Chain; Water; Snow; Earth; Fire | Progression options it rates lower overall. |

A dated article from a separate publisher, [Gordan Perisic's Destructoid comparison](https://www.destructoid.com/clover-time-tier-list/), was published on October 1, 2026 and modified on October 6. It similarly favors Anti Magic and Poison, with Ice, Explosive Flame, and Battle Lightning next. Its bottom groups differ: Chain, Water, and Snow are B-tier, while Earth and Fire are placed in its lowest group with a much harsher late-game assessment. This draft preserves that disagreement instead of merging the ratings.

[GAMES.GG's October 7 comparison](https://games.gg/roblox/guides/clover-time-grimoire-tier-list/), credited to Larc, lists the same ten names but places **Battle Lightning with Anti-Magic and Poison in S-tier**, **Chain and Explosive Flame in A**, **Ice and Water in B**, **Snow in C**, and **Fire and Earth in D**. It covers both PvP and PvE, unlike the narrower player-wiki comparison. These are its editorial placements, not an additional official tier system.

The source separates Explosive Flame from Fire. This distinction should be checked in the game rather than collapsed into one entry.

## Ten documented Grimoires and their reported rarity

The [public Grimoire Tower card](https://trello.com/c/KhpwU5Vn), independently read on October 9, 2026, groups ten linked book cards by rarity. The table below transcribes those groups, with the headings' spelling normalized. This is a public-board roster, not proof that every listed book remains obtainable in the current server build. Developer ownership of the board is still unconfirmed.

| Grimoire | Board-reported rarity |
| --- | --- |
| Earth | Common |
| Fire | Common |
| Snow | Common |
| Water | Common |
| Ice | Uncommon |
| Chain | Rare |
| Explosive Flame | Epic |
| Poison | Epic |
| Battle Lightning | Legendary |
| Anti Magic | Mythic |

These rarity groups describe the board's acquisition categories. They do not measure damage, guarantee a roll, or establish an individual book's drop probability. Keep **Fire** and **Explosive Flame** as separate entries.

## Compare published rankings by activity

Each column preserves its publisher's original tiers. Destructoid evaluates PvE; Gamezebo and GAMES.GG discuss both PvE and PvP. Their tiers are not interchangeable test results.

| Grimoire | Destructoid: PvE | Gamezebo: PvE/PvP | GAMES.GG: PvE/PvP |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Anti Magic | S | S | S |
| Poison | S | A | S |
| Battle Lightning | A | S | S |
| Explosive Flame | A | B | A |
| Ice | A | B | B |
| Chain | B | A | A |
| Water | B | B | B |
| Snow | B | C | C |
| Earth | Trash | D | D |
| Fire | Trash | D | D |

[Sho Roberts's Gamezebo article](https://www.gamezebo.com/walkthroughs/clover-time-grimoire-tier-list/), dated October 5, 2026, supplies the new middle column. It considers damage, skills, builds, and player consensus, but publishes no controlled encounters or measurements. Its A-tier Poison placement favors projectiles and continuing damage while keeping distance; its S-tier Battle Lightning placement favors use in both modes. These are the author's reasons, rather than this site's measured conclusions.

The strongest agreement is on Anti Magic. Poison, Battle Lightning, Chain, and Explosive Flame show why a recommendation should identify the activity and author instead of presenting one merged score. Agreement between articles does not establish that their underlying observations are independent.

## What criteria and limits apply?

The source evaluates movesets, damage, and usefulness in PvE. It supplies no controlled DPS measurements and makes no PvP ranking. This draft does not convert its editorial tiers into official values or this site's tested conclusions.

Its own examples show why context matters: it favors Poison for damage that continues during boss movement, Chain for control, and Snow's summons for farming. It distinguishes Anti Magic's base form from its reported awakened kit. Acquisition rarity does not alone establish how useful a book is for a particular activity.

Several claimed unlock conditions still need checks. In particular, the article calls Elf a "trait" while the site's race reference classifies Elf as a race, and the author it describes could not confirm a Battle Lightning move's availability. That requirement is not accepted here.

GAMES.GG says it tested the books but does not publish a test protocol or encounter results in the inspected article. Its table places Fire and Earth in D-tier, while a later callout says Earth is the only confirmed D-tier option. That inconsistency and the different PvP/PvE scope prevent treating the article as a decisive resolution of the other rankings.

## Which individual entries can be linked?

The [Anti-Magic research preview](/items/anti-magic/) and [Poison research preview](/items/poison/) contain the attributed ability descriptions behind this comparison. These are research pages, not accepted current-build gameplay tests. This page makes no recommendation to discard a book or spend resources solely on these untested tiers.

## What is this draft's evidence status?

This page remains a research draft. The cited articles and public Tower card were read on October 9, 2026. The player wiki supplies no publication date; Destructoid, Gamezebo, and GAMES.GG supply dates and authors. Their shared data's provenance is not established, and none was a gameplay test by this author. The table now provides a traceable documented roster and separate comparison criteria. Current-build availability, gameplay comparisons, and accepted entity pages for related links are still required.

> **Research preview.** This page contains source-attributed research, not a completed or independently play-tested guide. Unconfirmed steps and conflicting reports are marked below. Do not treat a reported code, cost, probability, or unlock condition as verified.

{/* P02: development research draft; excluded from production while draft is true. */}

![Original redeem concept illustration, not gameplay footage](/images/articles/clover-time/redeem-concept.webp)

*Original concept artwork, not a Clover Time screenshot or a depiction of verified items, characters, locations, or mechanics.*

![Original two reported code interfaces explanatory diagram, not an in-game screenshot](/images/articles/clover-time/how-to-redeem-codes-overview.svg)

## Where is the actual redemption field?

Two published screenshots were downloaded and visually inspected on October 9, 2026:

- [Beebom's redemption article](https://beebom.com/clover-time-codes/) shows the lobby with Afk World, Play, and Customize cards, plus a bottom-left Codes field with the placeholder "Enter code...".
- [Destructoid's redemption article](https://www.destructoid.com/clover-time-codes/) shows a montage: a lobby Codes field, an in-world Menu control, the menu's Settings option, and a Settings panel labeled Codes. Part of the input placeholder is cropped.

These images support two interface contexts. The earlier lobby-versus-Settings reports should no longer be treated as necessarily incompatible. The images do not show the click sequence running, code submission, or a successful result, and do not establish the current build.

## What sequence do the articles report?

Beebom says to use the lobby field and press Enter. Destructoid says the main menu has a code system and also describes Menu → Settings → code field → Enter while playing. The screenshots support the pictured controls; pressing Enter and receiving rewards remain article reports rather than observed actions.

## What conditions must a player meet?

Both articles report joining the AnimeCore Studio group. Beebom additionally reports completing the tutorial and restarting, while Destructoid says the main-menu system is accessible when entering the game. The inspected screenshots do not prove either account's eligibility conditions. Test those conditions separately rather than presenting them as a single established requirement list.

## What do failed redemption messages mean?

Capture the exact message. Distinguish an already-used code, an eligibility restriction, a typo, and confirmed expiry. Do not infer expiry from a generic failure.

## What is this draft's evidence status?

This page remains a verification draft. Beebom credits Sanmay Chakrabarti and was modified on October 6, 2026; Destructoid credits Ana Mitic and was modified on October 8. Those are article dates, not the screenshot capture dates or game versions. No game session, redemption, or eligibility test has been performed by this author. The inspected publisher images are cited for research and are not copied into this site's public assets.

> **Research preview.** This page contains source-attributed research, not a completed or independently play-tested guide. Unconfirmed steps and conflicting reports are marked below. Do not treat a reported code, cost, probability, or unlock condition as verified.

{/* P06: development research draft; excluded from production while draft is true. */}

![Original reroll concept illustration, not gameplay footage](/images/articles/clover-time/reroll-concept.webp)

*Original concept artwork, not a Clover Time screenshot or a depiction of verified items, characters, locations, or mechanics.*

![Original separate character categories explanatory diagram, not an in-game screenshot](/images/articles/clover-time/how-to-reroll-overview.svg)

*Original explanatory diagram. Source context and unconfirmed details are explained below.*

## Which attributes can actually be rerolled?

The [player wiki's reroll article](https://clovertime.wiki/progression/clover-time-rerolls), read on October 9, 2026, names Race, Social Class, and Trait as three separate reroll categories. Its race, class, and trait references use that same distinction. These are reported labels, not this author's observation of the live interface.

## Where does the source say to open rerolls?

The article describes two routes:

1. Open Menu at the top right, select Customize, then select Rolls or move between the attribute menus.
2. Speak to the Hage Priest inside the starting village's church to open the reroll menus.

The same article also mentions a spawn-house location in another recording. The user-provided beginner-video notes call the NPC High Priest. A separate screenshot below confirms Hage Priest in its pictured build, but the current NPC location and route from spawn remain unverified. The menu route is therefore a research lead, not an accepted current walkthrough.

## What does the published reroll interface show?

[Gamepur's race guide](https://www.gamepur.com/guides/clover-time-races-tier-list), by Aleksa Stojković and published October 5, 2026, supplies a screenshot actually inspected on October 9. Its heading reads **Hage Priest - Spins (2) - Special (0)**, with **Race**, **Social Class**, and **Trait** columns. Each column has **Roll** and **Get Special** buttons; the selected labels are Human, Commoner, and Fast Learner. The HUD shows **v0.10.41-T**.

This supports those labels in the pictured build. It shows two remaining Spins, not a cost of two Spins. It does not show a button press, a purchase, a warning, a balance deduction, or a changed result. It also does not locate the NPC from spawn.

Gamepur describes **Lobby → Customize → Rolls** in its text. That route has a different starting context from the in-world Menu route below; neither should be silently spliced into the other.

[Destructoid's tier-list article](https://www.destructoid.com/clover-time-tier-list/), published October 1, 2026 and modified October 6, also reports Menu → Customize → Rolls or speaking to the priest in the starting Hage church. This adds a dated report from another publisher, but no reroll confirmation or before-and-after result. Its top-right Menu placement also should not be assumed universal: Destructoid's separate codes montage pictures an in-world Menu control near the bottom left.

## What does a reroll consume?

The reroll article says all three categories share Spins and describes one Spin per attempt. It lists starting resources, playtime rewards, Index rewards, chests, codes, and purchases as possible supply sources. This author has not confirmed the current balance, reward intervals, or shop products.

The [Social Class](https://clovertime.wiki/progression/clover-time-social-classes) and [Trait](https://clovertime.wiki/progression/clover-time-traits) articles leave cost details undocumented. Reading them does not independently verify the reroll article's more specific cost claim. Inspect the actual category, displayed cost, and confirmation prompt before any attempt.

According to the site's [Mana Crystal article](https://clovertime.wiki/magic/clover-time-mana-crystals), Grimoire rolls use Mana Crystals instead of the character Spin pool. Calling both actions a "spin" does not establish that they consume the same inventory item.

## Does the new roll replace the old result?

The reroll article says the new result replaces the old one immediately; the class and trait articles describe replacement as well. None supplies the confirmation dialog or a recording this author has watched. A keep-old-result option, undo behavior, and lock or protection features remain unverified. This draft does not recommend rerolling a valued result.

The [public Clover Time Trello board](https://trello.com/b/XHcUunD7) lists storage gamepasses for Race, Social Class, and Trait, and its race cards distinguish normal from Special Spin odds. Those entries do not establish a free keep-old-result option or the current reroll warning. Do not infer preservation behavior or identical probability pools from the generic word "Spins."

## What is this draft's evidence status?

This page remains a verification draft. The player wiki has no article dates; Destructoid and Gamepur supply authors and article dates. Their agreement does not verify costs or preservation rules, and both publishers belong to the GAMURS network. Publication needs a current menu, exact cost and warning, and a before-and-after result. The screenshot supplies pictured menu labels, but not the missing transaction. No reroll has been performed by this author.

{/* P04: development research draft; excluded from production while draft is true. */}

![Original races concept illustration, not gameplay footage](/images/articles/clover-time/races-concept.webp)

*Original concept artwork, not a Clover Time screenshot or a depiction of verified items, characters, locations, or mechanics.*

![Original five board-reported races explanatory diagram, not an in-game screenshot](/images/articles/clover-time/race-tier-list-overview.svg)

*Original explanatory diagram. Source context and unconfirmed details are explained below.*

## Which race names are confirmed?

The [player wiki's race reference](https://clovertime.wiki/progression/clover-time-races), read on October 9, 2026, lists Human, Dwarf, Human-Dwarf, Elf, and Devil. These are source-reported names; this author has not checked the current game interface.

Sovereign should not be included in that race list: the same site's [Social Class reference](https://clovertime.wiki/progression/clover-time-social-classes) places it in a separate category. Its [Trait reference](https://clovertime.wiki/progression/clover-time-traits) separately lists Chosen One and Mana Sensitive. A recommended combination of these names is not a list of races.

## Which bonuses can be compared?

The public board supplies a qualitative comparison even where exact live values are unsettled. Each name below links to the card actually inspected, rather than to a search result.

| Race reference | Attributes described by its public card | Comparison use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Human](https://trello.com/c/1XRZZCkY) | Health, stamina, and mana regeneration; EXP. | Baseline regeneration and progression package. |
| [Dwarf](https://trello.com/c/MuEX9irS) | Health and stamina regeneration, stamina, mana, and mana regeneration; no EXP modifier listed. | Sustain and mana-capacity alternative. |
| [Human-Dwarf](https://trello.com/c/TRWJCKwx) | Health and stamina regeneration, stamina, mana, mana regeneration, and EXP. | Mixed sustain and progression package. |
| [Elf](https://trello.com/c/1jqSybCp) | Health and stamina regeneration, percentage and flat mana bonuses, mana regeneration, and EXP. | Mana-focused comparison. |
| [Devil](https://trello.com/c/HkmQFzgV) | Health, health and stamina regeneration, percentage and flat mana bonuses, mana regeneration, and EXP. | Broad passive package; its second-form requirement is a separate written claim. |

The Human-Dwarf card's title says **Human-Dwarf**, while its English description says **Half-Dwarf**. Published guides also write Human Dwarf. This page keeps the card-title convention without claiming that all three spellings are the current menu label. The inspected Dwarf, Elf, and Human-Dwarf card images show character appearances, not attribute panels; they do not settle the numerical disagreement.

The source describes health, stamina, mana, regeneration, and EXP modifiers. It reports different combinations for each race rather than one universal damage stat. This draft omits exact bonus values pending an independent interface check.

The source itself reports two different Devil roll chances from unnamed sessions. Neither a permanent probability nor an applicable game version is established by those readings.

The [public Clover Time Trello board](https://trello.com/b/XHcUunD7), read on October 9, 2026, has matching race cards but different Mana Regen values from the articles: its reported values are lower for all five races. It also separates normal and Special Spin chances. The board and articles do not establish a shared build, so this draft does not merge their numbers or infer a balance patch from the difference.

## Which passive values are visible in an actual screenshot?

On October 9, this author inspected the character-menu screenshot in [Gamepur's race article](https://www.gamepur.com/guides/clover-time-races-tier-list), published October 5, 2026. Its Race column selects **Human** and reads **+5% Health Regen, +5% Stamina Regen, +2.5% Mana Regen, +5% EXP**. The HUD identifies **v0.10.41-T**. Commoner and Fast Learner appear separately under Social Class and Trait.

These are screenshot observations for that capture, not a complete current five-race stat table. The same article's text gives Human **+5% Mana Regen**, disagreeing with its own pictured **+2.5%**. The picture matches the public board for Human, but does not verify the other four races. This is a reason to retain the numerical conflict, rather than choose the most frequently repeated table.

## What does a higher tier mean?

The [same site's race ranking](https://clovertime.wiki/tier-list/clover-time-races-tier-list) compares reported passive-stat packages; it explicitly says it did not measure leveling speed or DPS. Its placements are reproduced here as that site's judgment, rather than a ranking tested by this author.

| Reported tier | Race | Source's rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S | Devil | Broad regeneration, mana, and EXP bonuses. |
| A | Elf | Emphasis on mana capacity and recovery. |
| A | Human-Dwarf | Mixed regeneration and progression bonuses. |
| B | Dwarf | Sustain bonuses; the source lists no EXP bonus. |
| C | Human | Smaller baseline modifiers in the source's comparison. |

Those descriptions do not establish every activity's best race. Rarity alone also does not measure actual combat performance. This draft makes no recommendation to spend Spins chasing a particular result.

[Gordan Perisic's Destructoid article](https://www.destructoid.com/clover-time-tier-list/), published October 1, 2026 and modified October 6, lists the same five races and similar placements. It writes Human Dwarf without a hyphen and separates Sovereign into the Social Class column. This is corroboration from a separate publication, not proof that the two articles obtained their underlying data independently.

Gamepur also ranks Devil first and Elf second, but groups **Human-Dwarf and Dwarf together in B-tier**, unlike the player wiki's separate A/B placements. Its criterion is overall reported passive bonuses. It supplies no measured leveling comparison; its advice to reroll is not adopted here while transaction costs and retention remain unverified.

## What is this draft's evidence status?

This page remains a research draft. The player wiki supplies no article date or linked original recordings; Destructoid and Gamepur supply authors and article dates. They were read on October 9, 2026. A pictured Human label and its passives are now supported by an inspected screenshot. Its capture date and current applicability, the other races' attributes, and the numerical disagreement remain unresolved.

> **Research preview.** This page contains source-attributed research, not a completed or independently play-tested guide. Unconfirmed steps and conflicting reports are marked below. Do not treat a reported code, cost, probability, or unlock condition as verified.

{/* P07: development research draft; excluded from production while draft is true. */}

![Original fantasy concept illustration for anti magic, not gameplay footage](/images/articles/clover-time/anti-magic-concept.webp)

*Original concept artwork, not a Clover Time screenshot or a depiction of a verified route, weapon, or spell.*

![Original readable pc hud references explanatory diagram, not an in-game screenshot](/images/articles/clover-time/anti-magic-overview.svg)

*Original explanatory diagram. Source context and unconfirmed details are explained below.*

## Is Anti-Magic mentioned by the developer?

Yes. The official Roblox description includes the phrase “Awaken Anti-Magic.” This supports a mention of the feature, not a detailed ability list.

## How is it obtained and named in the interface?

The [player wiki's Anti-Magic article](https://clovertime.wiki/magic/clover-time-anti-magic-guide), read on October 9, 2026, describes obtaining it through the Grimoire Tower's random rolls, then equipping a sword-based kit. It calls the result Mythic and says the HUD meter changes to "anti-magic." This author has not checked those labels or the equipment controls in the game.

Its acquisition wording mixes "Spins" with Mana Crystals and suggests playtime rewards as a top-up. The same site's [Mana Crystal reference](https://clovertime.wiki/magic/clover-time-mana-crystals) explicitly separates character Spins from Grimoire currency. This draft does not treat the character Spin pool as payment for this book, publish roll probabilities, or assume a confirmed pity guarantee.

## Which abilities does the player wiki describe?

The [public Grimoire Tower roster](https://trello.com/c/KhpwU5Vn), read on October 9, places **Anti Magic** in its Mythic group and links its showcase card. Together with the pictured Tower prompt in [Gamepur's acquisition guide](https://www.gamepur.com/guides/how-to-get-grimoire-clover-time), this supports a reported Tower-roll acquisition category. The screenshot shows a crystal cost icon, but no Anti Magic result or equipment action. It does not establish a guaranteed route, drop chance, or successful acquisition by this author.

The article attributes move progression to Power rather than Strength. Its reported base kit includes:

| Reported name | Reported behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Anti-Magic Cut | An opening sword move. |
| Rush Divider | An attack that can hit multiple enemies. |
| Dual Spin | A held spinning attack. |
| Dash Divider | A lunge toward an enemy. |
| Counter | A response to an incoming hit. |
| Double Cut | A two-sword attack. |

These names and descriptions are third-party reports. Exact stat thresholds, damage, cooldowns, and platform controls are not established here. The source's approximate character level for one unlock is not a verified Power requirement.

## What does a published gameplay clip actually show?

The [public Trello Anti-Magic card](https://trello.com/c/18hQbOmI/104-anti-magia-anti-magic) links a short Anti Magic Cut demonstration. On October 9, 2026, this author downloaded the linked GIF and inspected frames at 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, and 3 seconds. Its PC HUD shows Anti Magic Cut with an E key label. The sequence shows a sword attack, impact effects, a hit indicator, and the target moving away.

That supports the pictured control and attack in this particular recording. It does not establish how to obtain or equip the book, a beginner's first unlock, current damage, or identical controls on other platforms. The clip's capture date and game version are unknown. The public card and player wiki also use differing names for some other moves; those labels need a separate interface check.

## Which additional PC labels are visible?

Two more GIFs linked by the [same public Anti-Magic card](https://trello.com/c/18hQbOmI) were downloaded and their sampled frames inspected on October 9. Their readable labels and the unresolved C-row label are separated below:

| HUD label | Pictured PC key | What the new samples establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anti Magic Cut | E | The label corroborates the earlier Cut demonstration. |
| Counter | X | The label corroborates the earlier Counter demonstration. |
| Name unreadable in the sampled frames | C | The bind is visible, but the low-resolution name cannot be established. |
| Dual Spin | Z | A visible HUD name and bind; a matching input is not shown. |
| Rush Divider | R | A visible HUD name and bind; the Rush sequence shows approach, close-range attacks, and hit indicators. |

The **Dual** file lasts 3.8 seconds. Samples at 0, 0.7, 1.5, 2.2, 3, and 3.7 seconds show the sword stance, a surrounding slash effect, and a hit indicator. The **Rush** file lasts 6.7 seconds; samples at 0, 1.3, 2.6, 4, 5.3, and 6.6 seconds show the approach and combat sequence. Neither displays the player's actual keypresses, so the file names alone are not used to identify every activated move. No damage, cooldown, or unlock threshold is derived from these samples.

The card text uses **Dual Slashes**, while the player wiki uses **Double Cut**. The sampled C-row HUD is too small to resolve the name reliably. Neither wording is presented as an independently read HUD label; their relationship across builds remains unresolved. These are third-party recordings with unknown capture dates and builds, not a test of current mobile or console controls.

## What is reported about Awakening?

The article says Devil is required for the Awakening, while distinguishing that requirement from equipping the base Grimoire. It describes a transformation, a replacement moveset, and meter consumption. The official description supports the existence of an Anti-Magic Awakening, but does not confirm these requirements or activation steps.

A complete unlock sequence and current activation control remain missing. This draft therefore does not promise that rolling Devil alone unlocks Awakening or instruct a player to spend resources pursuing it.

The same Trello card says a full bar and G trigger a second form, and its [Devil card](https://trello.com/c/HkmQFzgV/80-devil) says Devil is necessary for that form. Those are written card claims: the Cut frames inspected above do not demonstrate a transformation or its prerequisites.

## What do the additional Counter and transformation clips show?

This author inspected six sampled frames from each of two more GIFs linked by the same public card on October 9. The **Counter** clip is 4.1 seconds long: sampled frames at 0, 0.8, 1.6, 2.4, 3.2, and 4 seconds show **Counter — X** in the PC HUD, an exchange with a nearby target, a surrounding impact effect, and the target farther away afterward. A character input is not displayed, so this does not establish a tested activation window or guaranteed damage prevention.

The **Second Form** clip is 7.5 seconds long. Frames at 0, 1.5, 3, 4.5, 6, and 7.4 seconds show the starting sword stance, a red-and-black transformation animation, and a changed character appearance with a dark wing. Its gameplay HUD is hidden. It supports a transformation demonstration, but does not show a full meter, G being pressed, race selection, or the steps that unlocked it.

Both are third-party demonstrations with unknown capture dates and builds. They are distinct from this author's gameplay and do not resolve acquisition or Awakening prerequisites.

## What supports its placement in a tier list?

The [same site's PvE ranking](https://clovertime.wiki/tier-list/clover-time-grimoires-tier-list) places Anti Magic in its highest group, while noting limitations in the base kit's area attacks. This is its editorial judgment, not an official or independently tested tier. Its claimed chest-puzzle shortcut is also unverified by this author.

[Destructoid's dated comparison](https://www.destructoid.com/clover-time-tier-list/), published October 1, 2026 and modified October 6, also puts Anti Magic in its leading PvE group. It supports a separate publisher's ranking report, not the specific moves, stat requirements, or Awakening conditions described by the player wiki.

## What is this draft's evidence status?

This page remains an entity research draft. The player-wiki recordings are not linked, while the public Trello card supplies the Cut, Counter, transformation, Dual, and Rush GIFs whose sampled frames were inspected as described above. This author has not entered the game. Destructoid calls the board official, but a backlink from the confirmed Roblox developer has not been established. Current acquisition, equipment, remaining ability behavior, and the full Awakening path still need evidence.

The comparison describes Grimoire Tower rolls as the general book-acquisition system. It does not provide a complete Poison-specific acquisition record, a confirmed result screen, or equipment inputs. The board category above is attributed separately; no probability, unlock conditions, or guaranteed route is inferred from the general system description.

## What distinguishes its abilities?

The source describes three behaviors specific to Poison:

| Reported ability | Source's description |
| --- | --- |
| Poison spray | Damage continues while the player moves away from a boss. |
| Tox Explosion | A burst of poison damage. |
| Tox Clone | A summoned clone that can be commanded to attack NPCs. |

Those are attributed descriptions, not measured results. The article does not establish exact damage-over-time duration, stacking, command inputs, range, cooldowns, or skill requirements. No PvP performance is established.

The [public Trello Poison card](https://trello.com/c/ishInW3U/118-poison-grimoire), read on October 9, 2026, instead names Poison Bullet, Poison Mist, Toxic Explosion, and Toxic Clone. It describes Stop Clone and Order Clone commands. This adds a card-level reference, but the difference between Tox and Toxic labels remains unresolved without the current HUD. The card's incomplete cost lines and damage notation are not converted into a tested statistics table here.

The card's public JSON was also checked on October 9: it provides no attached images or clips. The written move list therefore cannot be described as independently watched Poison gameplay.

For a fuller written reference, the card distinguishes these four abilities. The behavior column translates its descriptions, without importing its incomplete cost or damage lines.

| Public-card name | Card-described behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Poison Bullet | Fires a poison projectile. |
| Poison Mist | Creates a mist that deals continuing damage to targets inside. |
| Toxic Explosion | Produces a poison explosion around the user. |
| Toxic Clone | Summons a fighting clone, with Stop Clone and Order Clone commands. |

Those descriptions separate the projectile, area damage, burst, and summon roles. They do not verify stacking, duration, command inputs, skill requirements, or a successful boss strategy. The [same player's Grimoire catalog](https://clovertime.wiki/magic/clover-time-grimoires), also read on October 9, uses Poison Mister, Tox Explosion, and Tox Clone instead. Exact HUD labels still require a readable Poison demonstration.

## Why does the source rate it highly?

[Sho Roberts's Gamezebo comparison](https://www.gamezebo.com/walkthroughs/clover-time-grimoire-tier-list/), dated October 5, places Poison in **A-tier**, below its S-tier Anti Magic and Battle Lightning. Its rationale is ranged projectiles and continuing damage for evasive play across PvE/PvP. Destructoid's narrower PvE ranking and GAMES.GG place Poison in S-tier. The different placements are kept separate; none supplies a published benchmark that proves a universal best book.

The player wiki places Poison in its top PvE group because of reported damage and move variety, with continuing damage as its boss-fight rationale. This draft does not claim that makes it universally best or interchangeable with Anti Magic's sword and transformation kit.
